thesis: No entry: the higher-timeframe trend and the immediate price action point in opposite directions, so no two independent evidence categories agree on one direction. All five watchlist contracts are in a clear daily uptrend (higher highs and higher lows, price well above the daily EMA20, 4h EMA20 above EMA50), which rules out a short on the complex. But the completed 00:00-04:00 UTC 4h bar rejected the 20-30 day range high on every one of the five, closing with a 43-71% upper wick on above-average volume (BTC tagged 81888 vs the 20-day high 81981.8; ETH tagged exactly 2700.0, its 30-day high; BNB tagged 784.94 vs its 20-day high 785.0), which rules out buying here. Derivatives are neutral rather than directional: funding is at or near the 0.010% baseline on BTC, SOL and XRP, 0.0058% on ETH and 0.0153% on BNB, with the next funding at 08:00 UTC, so there is no crowded positioning to fade or to ride. Market context is mildly bullish and therefore contradicts the short outright: alts are leading BTC over 24h (BNB +3.46%, ETH +2.93%, XRP +2.50%, SOL +2.18% against BTC +1.07%). The long also fails the reward/risk test on an honest stop: the best-looking candidate, BNB at 775.84 with the tightest spread on the board (0.52 bps), needs its stop below the last real higher low at 764.61 (1.45% risk, about 12.3 USDT net of the 14 bps round-trip cost estimate), which puts a 1.5 reward/risk target near 794, above the 785 high that has just rejected the whole complex on expanding volume. Placing the stop instead at 772.78 to buy a tighter risk would be choosing the stop to fit a position size, which the strategy prohibits. Separately, third-party reporting for today quotes BTC near 85,000 and ETH reclaiming 2,700-2,713 while the demo futures host this account trades on quotes BTC 81,427 and ETH 2,658.91, a material divergence, so external price levels were not used as evidence and only demo-host data was relied on. LESSONS.md currently holds no lessons (no closed trades yet), so no lesson made this decision more or less selective; the decision rests on the strategy's own entry conditions, in particular the two-independent-category rule, the 1.5 net reward/risk floor, the requirement that a stop sit on structure rather than on a desired size, and the instruction to prefer observation when conditions are unclear.
